---
title: "Systolic Blood Pressure and Gender Among Adults"
---

## Question

Among adults in the Neighborhood Health Survey, is systolic blood pressure associated with gender after accounting for age? The outcome is expressed in standard-deviation units, so the result can be compared with other outcomes on a common scale.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

survey <- read_csv(here::here("inputs/raw/neighborhood_health_survey.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Data

Adults are participants aged 18 and older. Blood pressure was measured only for examined participants, so the analysis keeps adults with a `systolic_mean` value. The group sizes are kept for the figure legend, and systolic pressure is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

```{r}
adults <- survey |>
  filter(age_years >= 18, !is.na(systolic_mean)) |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  mutate(
    n_in_group = n(),
    systolic_z = as.numeric(scale(systolic_mean))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(gender_label = paste0(gender, " (n = ", format(n_in_group, big.mark = ","), ")"))

n_adults <- sum(survey$age_years >= 18)
n_analyzed <- nrow(adults)
```

The survey has `r format(n_adults, big.mark = ",")` adults. Of these, `r format(n_analyzed, big.mark = ",")` have a blood pressure measurement and are included.

## Sample by gender

Men and women have a similar age distribution, so age adjustment should change little.

```{r}
adults |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(age_years),
    sd_age = sd(age_years)
  )
```

## Model

A linear regression of standardized systolic pressure on age and gender. Women are the reference group.

```{r}
fit <- lm(systolic_z ~ age_years + gender, data = adults)

coefs <- tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
coefs

age_per_decade <- 10 * coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "age_years"]
gender_diff <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "gendermale"]
gender_ci <- coefs[coefs$term == "gendermale", c("conf.low", "conf.high")]
gender_p <- coefs$p.value[coefs$term == "gendermale"]
```

## Figure

```{r}
#| message: false
ggplot(adults, aes(x = age_years, y = systolic_z, color = gender_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Systolic blood pressure rises with age at the same level for men and women",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Systolic blood pressure (SD units)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Interpretation

Systolic blood pressure is strongly associated with age: each additional decade is associated with `r round(age_per_decade, 2)` SD higher systolic pressure, holding gender constant. After accounting for age, men and women do not differ meaningfully in systolic blood pressure. The estimated difference is `r round(gender_diff, 2)` SD (95% CI `r round(gender_ci$conf.low, 2)` to `r round(gender_ci$conf.high, 2)`, p = `r round(gender_p, 2)`).

The analysis is unweighted and ignores the survey design, so the estimates describe this sample. The data are simulated for teaching.
